children: Max Healthcare unveiled its new 400-bed state-of-the-art Saket facility in Delhi on Thursday as it presses ahead with a plan to more than double capacity, while keeping the door open for acquisitions and additional borrowing to fund growth.
Chairman and Managing Director Abhay Soi told Moneycontrol that the company intends to continue pursuing M&A opportunities and is comfortable increasing leverage from current levels.
Delhi's biggest private healthcare campus

The new facility, inaugurated by Home Minister Amit Shah, takes the Saket complex’s capacity to around 1,200 operational beds, making it one of the largest private healthcare campuses in the capital. A further 600-bed expansion is planned at the same campus over the next three to four years, taking the census bed count to about 1,800.

Even as Max invests aggressively in brownfield and greenfield projects, Soi said the company remains firmly in acquisition mode and is willing to increase leverage substantially from current levels to pursue opportunities.

“My target is that I operate near 2.5 times debt to EBITDA. Right now, we are less than 1 time debt to EBITDA,” Soi told Moneycontrol. “We started the year well. We did acquisitions... and we intend to.”

That stance is consistent with management commentary to investors, where Max has highlighted a “robust deal pipeline”, strong free cash flow generation and “adequate headroom for M&A driven by strong free cash flows and low leverage”. The company ended June with net debt of Rs 2,384 crore and a net debt-to-EBITDA ratio below 1.

Soi said the current expansion programme, which aims to take Max’s capacity to more than 10,000 beds over the next few years, can be funded through internal accruals, reducing the need for fresh equity.
“For this phase expansion, going up to 10,000 beds, we will be funding it through internal accruals. We are investing all the free cash flows that we make to build new capacities,” he said.
Around 4,000 beds are expected to be added over the next three to four years.
Soi added that Max is investing more than Rs 6,000 crore on capex.
Acquisitions remain a key pillar
Max generated free cash flow of Rs 397 crore in the June quarter and reiterated its strategy of deploying cash towards capacity expansion and acquisitions.
On acquisitions, Soi indicated Max is not restricted by geography or asset size and would consider regional hospital chains if returns meet its thresholds.

“I’m okay with all acquisitions,” he said, adding that the company looks at around 20-21 cities across India and is currently present in nine. “We are not selective on geographies. North, East, West... all in India only.”

The company recently acquired Kalinga Hospital in Bhubaneswar and has also acquired projects in Pune, while earlier acquisitions in Lucknow, Noida and Nagpur are now entering capacity expansion phases.
New facilities won't be a drag on margins

At the newly opened Saket facility, Soi said Max has focused on robotics, artificial intelligence and premium patient infrastructure aimed at both domestic and international patients. Around 40 percent of Delhi patients come from outside NCR, while international patients contribute roughly 9 percent of business.

Beyond Saket, Max plans to add about 100 beds in Lucknow and commission a 500-bed hospital in Gurugram by the end of FY27. The company is also expanding in Mumbai, Mohali, Dwarka, Pitampura and other markets.
Despite the heavy expansion pipeline, Soi remains confident that margins will hold up because nearly 70 percent of upcoming capacity is brownfield, where occupancy ramps up quickly.
“Majority is 70 percent brownfield,” he said, noting that recently opened brownfield projects are already seeing occupancy levels approaching 80 percent.

title: Abhay Soi says Max Healthcare has room to double down on M&A even as capex tops Rs 6,000 crore
